body:
P2-12 PLAN 4/6: TYPO FORGIVING (N-23b), the traps and the rules (replaces the first version of this note)
One measure, on the server, after P2-25 and the slice-4 drawing. Folded text (P2-25's normaliser, every script kept), then an optimal-string-alignment distance: a letter wrong, missing, extra or two neighbours swapped costs 1 (the shipped rule, artist_typo.dart); a look-alike pair of a SYMBOL and a letter costs 0. Allowance = the shipped one: none when the shorter of the two has under 5 letters, 1 edit for 5 to 8, 2 from 9. A symbol is not an edit: "P!nk" is distance 0 from "pink", accepted at any length although a 4-letter name is never guessed by edits.
CORRECTION (advisor): letter-for-letter pairs are NOT look-alikes. v~a, v~u and k~c at cost 0 would make "Corn" match "Korn": guesses on short names the rule forbids. They are ordinary edits; "landmarks" to "landmvrks" is ONE edit on a 9-letter name (allowance 2). k~c is a sound-alike: dropped.
TRAP 1, order. The normaliser removes punctuation, so "Ke$ha" would become "ke ha" and "P!nk" "p nk". The distance runs on a form that keeps $ @ ! 0 to 9 and the other symbols of the table (only white space and . , ' " - _ & ( ) are dropped), and the pairs apply to BOTH sides: the typed text and every candidate name.
TRAP 2, reach. "landmarks" contains no symbol to swap, so no swap in the typed text produces "landmvrks". It is found only by comparing the typed text with NAMES THE SERVER KNOWS (the library's artists, from song_ref lead and album artists of songs with files; the names in artist_catalogue; the artist names in the last 2,000 cached answers), and then asking the catalogue for THAT name's own spelling. An artist the server has never seen and Deezer does not return for the typed text stays NOT FOUND: say so, and put one such expected miss in the N-16 typo set. "metalica" already works through Deezer itself (lead's check, 14 Nov): the server does not ask again.
THE TABLE (short, hand-written, symmetric pairs at cost 0, no dependency): $ s, @ a, ! i, 0 o, 1 i and 1 l, 3 e, 4 a, 5 s, 7 t. The letters NFKD does not decompose (o with stroke, ae, oe, sharp s, d with stroke, l with stroke, thorn, eth) are folded to their Latin spelling: a fold, not a guess.
WHEN IT FIRES AND THE CAP. Only after the three primary requests answered and NO artist, album or song name in them is within the allowance of the typed text (a search the catalogue already answers costs nothing extra). At most TWO extra outside requests, inside the search's ceiling of 7, cached like any answer: (1) the nearest known name's own spelling; (2) the typed text with its symbols spelt out ("ke$ha" -> "kesha"). Never while the breaker is resting. Songs and albums: only artists have a dictionary; songs and albums rely on the catalogue's own fuzziness (extend to cached album titles if the 40-search set shows a gap).
"SHOWING RESULTS FOR ...": the primary results for the person's words are ALWAYS in the answer, untouched; extra rows carry assumed: true; the answer has interpretedAs {text, kind: known-name | symbols} only when something was assumed. The server never replaces the person's words and the phone never changes the field. ONE quiet line above the lists (wording decided by the drawing; suggestion: Also showing results for "Landmvrks"); assumed rows score below every exact answer. A new S-12 state: DRAWN FIRST (slice 4).
MEASURED, not guessed: N-16's 40 searches get a typo section of about 15 rows with the expected hit and rank: Landmvrks/landmarks (via the library's own name), Hozier/hosier, Ke$ha/kesha, P!nk/pink, Sigur Ros, Motley Crue, suicideboys/$uicideboy$; expected misses that pin the rules (a 1-letter typo in a 4-letter name; "Corn" for "Korn"; two edits in a 5-letter name; an artist never seen by the server and not returned by Deezer). The same typo-rule.json is run by the Dart test (artist_typo_test) and tests/test_catalogue_forgive.py: the one place two implementations of one rule are accepted.
